title: Sensitivity-driven INT8 SmoothQuant automation and runtime kernel shims
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build an automated calibration and validation pipeline that produces sensitivity-driven per-layer INT8 quantization profiles using SmoothQuant-style activation scaling, and provide small runtime kernel shims to enable safe fallback and minimal-impact rollouts. The goal is to produce deployable profiles that achieve <=1% eval metric regression vs FP16 on our standard eval suite for large transformer models while keeping inference throughput improvements consistent across common infra (A100, H100).
background: We have several calibration and runtime efforts (multiple tickets listing various calibration harnesses and kernel adapters). Teams have prototypes for smooth-activation scaling but lack an end-to-end automation that: 1) produces per-workload quant profiles, 2) validates quality against our eval suite, 3) emits runtime-compatible profile artifacts and shim code for the kernel selector, and 4) provides telemetry-driven autotune suggestions. Current experiments show good results on small models but uneven regressions on KV-cache-heavy workloads.
proposal: 1) Build a sensitivity analyzer that measures activation vs weight sensitivity per layer using a small set of representative prompts (prompt bank stored in Drive). 2) Generate candidate SmoothQuant scaling maps and run an automated calibration pass to produce INT8 scales/zero-points and per-layer fallback thresholds. 3) Add lightweight runtime kernel shims that accept profile metadata (scale map + tolerance) and can switch kernels or force partial-FP16 for layers exceeding thresholds. 4) Integrate with CI: new cal profiles get gated by automated eval runs; profiles that pass are uploaded to the calibration store and surfaced to the model catalog as 'validated-int8' variants. 5) Add telemetry to Redwood Console for per-route accuracy drift and automatic requeue for re-calibration when drift exceeds thresholds.
acceptance_criteria:
- Automated pipeline runs end-to-end on at least two models (Llama-2-7B, Llama-2-13B) and emits validated-int8 profiles.
- Eval regression <=1.0% on perplexity and <=2.0 BLEU/ROUGE relative to FP16 on our standard prompt bank.
- Runtime kernel shim demonstrates safe channel to fallback with <3% p50 latency regression when fallback triggered.
- CI gate prevents merging profiles that fail validation.
- Documentation for profile format and shim API published in Drive and referenced from model catalog.
tasks: Design sensitivity analyzer (Avery) - define metrics and prompt samples
Implement calibration harness extension (Ravi) - pipeline to run candidate scale maps and produce profile artifacts
Create profile schema v2 (binary+json) and uploader to calibration store (Infra)
Implement runtime shim API (Ravi) - kernel selector hooks and fallback call paths
Run large-scale validation runs (Perf team) - L2-7B and L2-13B across A100/H100
Integrate CI gating and automerge rules for validated profiles
Docs: design doc and runbook for re-calibration cadence
risks_mitigations: Risk: Calibration results are brittle across prompt banks. Mitigation: maintain small stratified prompt bank + out-of-sample validation set and require pass on both.
Risk: Kernel shim introduces latency jitter. Mitigation: microbenchmark shim overhead and keep shim logic inlined; use per-layer cold-start warmup to prefetch kernels.
Risk: Profiles lead to silent quality regressions in production. Mitigation: add console telemetry and automatic rollback policy based on degraded route-level metrics.
Risk: Hardware variance between A100/H100. Mitigation: run calibration on both infra types and tag profiles with 'tested_on' metadata.
Risk: Security/compat issues with profile uploads. Mitigation: sign profiles and require uploader IAM role; record audit log entries.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal validation - run pipeline on test fleet, manual inspection of top-5 failure cases (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Canary - expose validated-int8 profiles as opt-in variant for a small set of internal customers; monitor drift and latency (4 weeks).
Phase 3: Gradual rollout - model catalog exposes validated-int8 with explicit fallback policy and 10% traffic route canary (2 weeks).
Phase 4: Full release - flip default to validated-int8 for eligible routes with documented caveats (depends on pass metrics).
test_plan: Unit tests for sensitivity analyzer and profile serializer
Regression harness: run standard eval suite (perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE, accuracy) for every candidate profile
Performance microbenchmarks for kernel shim across sequence lengths (32/512/2048) and KV-cache hot paths
Chaos test: simulate kernel unavailable path and verify deterministic fallback behavior
End-to-end CI job that fails merge if eval regression above thresholds
notes: 2025-01-10 - Avery Chen: Created ticket. Prototype sensitivity script produced layerwise sensitivity scores for L2-7B using 200 prompts. Observed that early feedforward layers dominate activation sensitivity.

2025-01-17 - Ravi Patel: Implemented initial candidate generator for scale maps. Initial INT8 calibration on L2-7B produced 0.6% perplexity regression vs FP16 but 3.1% on KV-cache-heavy chat traces. Hypothesis: attention projection scaling needs special handling for past_key_value reuse.

2025-01-22 - Perf Team (notes): Ran baseline on A100 and H100. Throughput improvements of 1.7-2.2x observed for most configs, but slight p95 latency increase when shim performed dynamic kernel swap on sequence>1024. Action: add pre-warm path for common kernel sizes.

2025-01-29 - Design Review: Agreed on profile format v2: JSON metadata (checksums, tested_on, tolerance thresholds) + binary packed table for per-layer scales. Document link: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/smoothquant-profile-v2
2025-02-05 - Ravi Patel: Kernel shim API sketch landed in repo, PR #1234. Shim exposes 'profile_tolerance_check' and 'force_fp16_for_layer' entrypoints. Still need CI gating and uploader integration.
